title: MOSFET Parameters
summary: what the key MOSFET datasheet numbers mean and the calculations they feed: conduction loss, junction temperature, gate drive, and power derating.
body:
a MOSFET datasheet lists many ratings; a handful drive almost every design
decision. the ratings are the stored inputs -- most of what you actually want
(will it survive, how hot, how fast) is calculated from them.

V_DS is the maximum drain-source voltage the device blocks when off; stay well
under it (allow margin for switching spikes). V_GS(th) is the gate threshold
where the channel starts to conduct -- a standard MOSFET needs ~10 V on the
gate for its rated R_DS(on), while a logic-level part reaches it at 3-5 V. this
is the single most common beginner trap: driving a standard MOSFET from a 3.3 V
or 5 V pin leaves it half-on and dissipating heat. R_DS(on) is the on-resistance
(always quoted at a specific V_GS); it sets conduction loss. I_D is the rated
continuous drain current, but note it is specified at an idealized case
temperature -- the real current limit is almost always thermal, set by R_th and
your heatsink, not by the headline I_D. Q_g is the total gate charge; it sets
how much current the gate driver must supply to switch in a given time. R_th(JC)
and R_th(JA) are the junction-to-case and junction-to-ambient thermal
resistances that turn dissipated watts into a temperature rise.

formulas.description: conduction loss when fully on -- the dominant loss in low-frequency (DC/slow PWM) switching
junction temperature with no heatsink (still air). keep T_j below the datasheet max (often 150-175 C)
junction temperature referenced to the case (use with a heatsink; add the case-to-sink and sink-to-air resistances for the full chain)
average gate-drive current needed to switch the device in time t_sw (sets the gate driver and gate resistor)
real dissipation ceiling at a given case temperature -- the headline P_D assumes T_c = 25 C, which almost never holds

examples: IRF520 switching 4 A continuously: P_cond = 4^2 * 0.27 = 4.3 W. with R_th(JA) ~ 62 C/W and no heatsink, that is a ~270 C rise -- impossible, so it needs a heatsink or far less current. this is why the headline 9.2 A rating is misleading without thermal design.

logic-level check: a standard MOSFET (V_GS(th) up to 4 V) driven from a 3.3 V pin never fully turns on; R_DS(on) is far above the 10 V spec and it overheats. pick a logic-level part or add a gate driver.
gotchas: R_DS(on) is always specified at a stated V_GS -- a value at V_GS=10 V does not apply if you drive the gate to 5 V
the continuous I_D rating assumes an unrealistic case temperature; in practice thermal resistance and your heatsink set the usable current, not I_D
V_GS(th) is where conduction begins, not where the device is fully on; full enhancement needs the V_GS at which R_DS(on) is specified
for fast PWM, add switching loss (from Q_g, capacitances and switching times) to the conduction loss; at DC/slow speeds conduction loss dominates
